title: THE CONSISTENCY-ACCEPTABILITY DIVERGENCE OF LLMS IN JUDICIAL DECISION-MAKING: TASK AND STAKEHOLDER DIMENSIONS

bias_targets.methodology: Systematic review of public opinion surveys and empirical studies assessing public trust in AI-assisted judges across different racial/ethnic groups and evaluating the risk of AI perpetuating historical biases against minority communities.
Analysis of survey data and legal practice reports regarding the potential for new systemic inequalities when high-quality AI legal services require payment, negatively impacting low-income groups.

Review of empirical data evaluating the lack of inclusive design and accessibility features in court LLM tools, assessing their inability to accommodate the special needs of disabled persons in legal proceedings.
Analysis of case studies and acceptance data regarding elderly individuals' lack of acceptance and concerns over AI technologies (e.g., deepfakes) in court proceedings.

Conceptual analysis of the human cognitive tendency to over-rely on mechanically consistent LLM outputs in judicial tasks, where users fail to identify errors without knowing the correct answer beforehand.
